doc.title: Jackie Cain and Roy Kral interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, March 22, 1998

title: Leaving Riverdale and buying the Montclair house
summary: The Nadelman son returns, they search for houses, and find their present home, moving in May 1, 1973.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Finally the owner of the house in Riverdale came back, he was in the Foreign Service, the son of Elie Nadelman, it was Jan Nadelman, he came back and we knew that it’s time. Our tenure is up, we’re not going to be here anymore. And we started house hunting. Well we looked in Nyack, we looked in Westchester, we looked here we looked there, we were so spoiled, having this huge property and trees, and view of the river and private drive. So now we can’t find anything that we can afford.
Of course the old furniture that we’d picked up that fit in the house.

Friends of ours lived in Montclair and says, “when you’re through house hunting, come by for dinner so you can relax and you don’t have to be so depressed about not finding anything.” So we’re looking around Montclair, and we say gee, that looks nice, this is nice, we started to get the New York Times and picked it up on Sunday, looked at it, go out to Montclair, and get there, and finally we get there, and the ones we wanted were gone. We would get the New York Times on a Saturday and look, and circle things and call up the real estate agent, meet him there on a Sunday morning. Now we’re in business. We looked here, there, this house, that house, that house. We walked into the house we now have, in 1973, the real estate agent was in front of me, I was behind her and Jackie was behind me. We walked in the door of this place and here’s a great center hall, you step up and there’s more hall and there’s colonial center hall construction.
Don’t go through all that Roy.
And Jackie is behind me and she pulls my coat and she says — [whispers] “This is it, this is it.”
I knew right away, I could see the quality of the house, and the way it was constructed. He did too.
And we gave notice to our place there. They were happy to have us out and we moved in to this new place on May 1, 1973.
